text: Which of the 2026 Nobel laureates in Physiology or Medicine is a professor at the University of Würzburg, and at which Max Planck Institute (and in which city) did he lead the research group where the light-gated channels were discovered?

Nagel led an independent research group at the Max Planck Institute of Biophysics in Frankfurt am Main (1992-2004), where channelrhodopsins were characterised. (chain: 2026 Nobel medicine laureates -> Würzburg laureate -> his earlier institute) Partly correct: Nagel right but institute or city wrong (e.g. MPI for Brain Research). text: List every SpaceX Starship flight test launched between 1 January and 30 September 2026, with the launch date and the main outcome of each flight.
reference: Answer (3 flights, all Block 3 from Starbase Pad 2): Flight 12, 22 May 2026 (B19/S39), first Block 3 flight: partial success; booster lost an engine, flipped the wrong way at hot staging and failed its Gulf landing, ship completed its flight and splashed down. Flight 13, 24 July 2026 (after a 16 July post-ignition abort and a 23 July weather scrub): suborbital, carried 20 real Starlink V3 satellites, ship made a controlled splashdown intact; counted a success. Flight 14, 28 September 2026 12:48 UTC (B21/S41, mission 'Starlink Group 31-1'): first Starship to reach orbit, deployed 26 Starlink V3 satellites, first commercial Starship flight. Grading: correct = all three flights with right dates (±1 day) and the key outcome of each (F14 = first orbital + Starlink deployment); partly = 2 of 3, or all three with a wrong/missing outcome; wrong = misses Flight 14 or lists 2025 flights (Flights 10/11) as 2026. SpaceNews called the 23/24 Sep missions China's 9th and 10th of the month and put China at 70 orbital attempts for 2026. Grading: correct = at least 9 of the 10 with right vehicles and no invented launches; partly = 6-8; wrong = 5 or fewer, or mixes in non-Chinese launches. text: Which new orbital rockets (or new variants) made their first launch attempt between 1 January and 30 September 2026? Give the rocket, country, date and whether the maiden flight succeeded.

text: Under the FCC order of June 2026 on Amazon Leo (Kuiper) missing its July 30, 2026 half-deployment milestone, did the FCC grant Amazon's requested 24-month extension? Give the order number, how many satellites the milestone required, and the condition the FCC imposed instead.
reference: Answer: No extension. The Space Bureau's Order DA 26-553 (adopted/released 5 June 2026, file SAT-MOD-20260129-00065) instead granted a limited, conditional WAIVER of the 50% milestone (47 CFR 25.164(b)(1)) and the automatic-termination rule. Milestone = 1,616 satellites (half of 3,232 Gen1). Condition: satellites not deployed by 30 July 2026 temporarily lose their processing-round priority (2020 Ka/Ku and 2021 V-band rounds) until the earlier of 20 months after 30 July 2026 (30 March 2028) or the date Amazon reaches 50% deployment; this can be shortened to 15 months (30 Oct 2027) if Amazon certifies it has built the satellites and procured launches. Final 100% milestone (30 July 2029) unchanged. Partly correct: says waiver granted with spectrum-priority demotion but wrong/missing numbers or order id; or uses 1,618/3,236 (older pre-modification counts) with otherwise correct conditions. Wrong: says extension to 2028 granted, or says no relief/license revoked. Sources: https://docs.fcc.gov/public/attachments/DA-26-553A1.txt ; https://www.benton.org/headlines/fcc-grants-kuipers-request-extend-or-waive-interim-milestone

text: Which exact frequency bands did the FCC approve transferring from EchoStar to SpaceX in May 2026? List each band with its MHz ranges and give the FCC document number and date.
reference: Answer: Memorandum Opinion and Order DA 26-471 (Wireless Telecommunications Bureau and Space Bureau, adopted and released 12 May 2026). Bands to SpaceX: AWS-4 2000-2020 MHz and 2180-2200 MHz (40 MHz); AWS H Block 1915-1920 MHz and 1995-2000 MHz (10 MHz); unpaired AWS-3 1695-1710 MHz (up to 15 MHz); ~65 MHz total, deal ~$17B, for direct-to-device use. Partly correct: names AWS-4 + H-block + AWS-3 and ~65 MHz but wrong/missing frequency ranges or document number; or describes 2 GHz/AWS-4 only. Wrong: says the 3.45 GHz or 600 MHz licenses went to SpaceX (those went to AT&T), or that the deal was not approved. Sources: https://docs.fcc.gov/public/attachments/DA-26-471A1.txt ; https://www.advanced-television.com/2026/05/13/fcc-approves-echostars-spectrum-sale-to-spacex-att/

text: How many Starship-Super Heavy launches per year have been environmentally approved at Kennedy's LC-39A (FAA record of decision, January 2026) and at Cape Canaveral's SLC-37 (Department of the Air Force record of decision, November 2025)?

SLC-37: up to 76 launches and 152 landings per year; DAF ROD signed 20 Nov 2025, contingent on an FAA supplemental airspace analysis. Partly correct: one of the two numbers right. Wrong: gives Starbase's 25/year for either site, or swaps the numbers. Sources: https://policyrisk.com/federal-register/2026-02108 ; https://public-inspection.federalregister.gov/2025-23314.pdf

text: In the European Commission's first-ever Digital Services Act non-compliance decision against X (December 2025), how was the total fine split across the individual infringements, and which DSA articles were breached?
reference: Answer: Total EUR 120 million, decision 5 Dec 2025: EUR 45m for the deceptive paid blue checkmark (Art. 25(1), dark patterns), EUR 40m for failing to give researchers access to public data (Art. 40(12)), EUR 35m for the non-transparent advertising repository (Art. 39). X got 60 working days (checkmark) and 90 working days (action plan for ads/researcher access). Partly correct: correct EUR 120m and three infringements but no or wrong per-item split, or missing article numbers. Wrong: wrong total (e.g. the rumoured ~$1bn), or describes the Jan 2026 Grok proceedings as the fine. Sources: https://heise.de/-11104571 ; https://www.scottishlegal.com/articles/x-fined-eur120-million-for-breaches-of-eu-digital-services-act

text: The EU's 'Digital Omnibus on AI' amending the AI Act was published in 2026. What is its regulation number, when was it published in the Official Journal, from when do stand-alone (Annex III) high-risk obligations now apply, and from when is the new Article 5 ban on AI systems generating non-consensual intimate imagery or CSAM applicable?
reference: Answer: Regulation (EU) 2026/1744, published in the OJ on 24 July 2026 (in force a few days later; EP final vote 16 June 2026). Annex III high-risk obligations: 2 December 2027 (was 2 Aug 2026); Annex I/embedded high-risk: 2 August 2028. New prohibited practice (AI generating CSAM / non-consensual intimate material): applies from 2 December 2026. Partly correct: correct high-risk dates but missing/wrong regulation number or ban date; or says 'adopted mid-2026' without OJ date. Wrong: says the omnibus is still only a proposal, or gives 2 Aug 2026 as the Annex III date. Sources: https://www.cuatrecasas.com/en/global/intellectual-property/art/digital-omnibus-ai-has-been-published ; https://fpf.org/blog/the-ai-act-implementation-timeline-what-changes-under-the-ai-omnibus/

text: In its July 2026 Upper C-band order, which exact frequency range did the FCC make available for terrestrial wireless, how is the band split into licenses (block size and license area), and what is the order's FCC number?
reference: Answer: 3.98-4.14 GHz (160 MHz) for flexible terrestrial use, with a 4.14-4.16 GHz guard band (satellite stays above); eight 20-MHz unpaired blocks licensed by Partial Economic Area (PEA), contiguous US; Report and Order FCC 26-46 adopted 22 July 2026. Creates a 440 MHz 3.7-4.14 GHz 'super band'; auction must be complete by July 2027; transition deadlines 30 Dec 2030 (top 75 PEAs) and 30 June 2031. Partly correct: 160 MHz / 3.98-4.14 GHz right but wrong block structure or missing FCC number; or says 'about 100+ MHz of 3.98-4.2 GHz'. Wrong: whole 3.98-4.2 GHz (220 MHz) auctioned, or confuses with the 2021 Auction 107 (3.7-3.98 GHz). Sources: https://www.dwt.com/blogs/broadband-advisor/2026/07/fcc-adopts-upper-c-band-transition-order ; https://www.telecomstechnews.com/news/fcc-votes-on-160mhz-upper-c-band-auction-for-5g-and-6g/

text: Ireland's Data Protection Commission has opened two GDPR inquiries into X Internet Unlimited Company related to Grok. What does each one cover and when was each opened?

(2) Notified to XIUC 16 Feb 2026, announced 17 Feb 2026: the creation and publication on X of potentially harmful non-consensual intimate and/or sexualised images (incl. of children) generated with Grok (principles, lawfulness, data protection by design). Partly correct: describes only one of the two inquiries correctly, or both topics without dates. Wrong: says the DPC has fined X over Grok, or confuses it with the EU Commission's DSA probe (26 Jan 2026) or Ofcom's (12 Jan 2026). Sources: https://www.dataprotection.ie/en/news-media/latest-news/data-protection-commission-announces-commencement-inquiry-x-internet-unlimited-company-xiuc ; https://www.rte.ie/news/business/2026/0217/1558842-grok-ireland/
